question: Recent publications reveal serious allegations12 regarding the management of programmes in the fields of education, youth and lifelong learning, several of which are financed by EU funds.

According to the publications, the ruling party's youth members hold positions both in the administration of the competent national body and in companies that received contracts or participated in assignments within the framework of the relevant programmes, while - in the case of tenders - the same persons are allegedly connected to competing companies.

The case raises reasonable questions regarding conflicts of interest, embezzlement of European funds, the transparency of award processes and the effectiveness of the control mechanisms that the Member State must implement3. In light of the above: 1.

Does the Commission intend to request explanations from the Greek authorities regarding the management, award procedures and controls carried out in the specific programmes, taking into account the complaints?

What supervisory and assurance tools can the Commission activate within the framework of its competences in order to verify that the Member State complies with EU obligations on the prevention of conflicts of interest, transparency and sound financial management?

Does the Commission intend to request detailed information from the Greek authorities on expenditure, awards, participation of companies and control procedures in order to assess compliance with the rules governing the protection of the Union's financial interests?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.3.2026) The Erasmus+ programme is committed to promoting equal opportunities and access, inclusiveness, and fairness across its actions while also adhering strictly to regulations that ensure fair and transparent management.

When the Commission becomes aware of any suspected cases of fraud, corruption or other illegal activities affecting the EU budget, it informs the European Anti-Fraud Office and, where applicable, the European Public Prosecutor’s Office. In this specific case, the Commission is actively verifying the matter with the Youth and Lifelong Learning Foundation.

The Commission has requested comprehensive explanations from the Foundation regarding their management practices, award procedures and oversight activities. This approach aims to ensure compliance with EU obligations and the protection of the reputation of EU-funded initiatives across Member States.
Should there be any indications of potential fraud, corruption or other illegal activities affecting the EU budget, the Commission will refer the matter to the competent investigative bodies.
